cell_type: inferred: The uncultured gammaproteobacterial Riftia symbiont, a single 16S rRNA phylotype tentatively named “Candidatus Endoriftia persephone”, densely populates bacteriocytes in the host trophosome, a specialized organ that fills most of the worm’s body cavity.
material_type: Riftia specimens were dissected onboard, and samples from four different organs (here referred to as tissues) were stored at –80°C: the lamellae of the tentacular crown were shaved off to provide plume samples, trophosome samples were dissected from whole trophosome, body wall samples were retrieved and washed after removal of the trophosome, and vestimental samples were cut off from the lateral portions of the vestimentum.
sample_source: Riftia specimens were collected by the human occupied vehicle Alvin or the remotely operated vehicle Jason in approximately 2,500-m water depth.
species: One of the most conspicuous representatives of these associations, and the first animal in which chemoautotrophic symbionts were discovered, is the giant tube worm Riftia pachyptila (short Riftia), which thrives around deep-sea hydrothermal vents of the East Pacific.
tissue: Trophosome tissue containing large amounts of stored sulfur has a light yellowish color.
